content: The green reed which bends in the wind is stronger than the mighty oak which breaks in a storm.
author: Marcus Aurelius
story:
At its core, this reflection cuts through our everyday excuses. Hardship is not an unfair interruption to your real life—it is the very forge in which character is tempered. No one develops deep wisdom, empathy, or stamina by cruising down an easy path without resistance.

In Marcus Aurelius's view, genuine strength is not an abstract theory—it is a lived, daily practice. Like a tree that develops deeper roots when buffeted by winter gales, your past trials gave you a reservoir of strength you didn't know you possessed. You are more durable than your anxious thoughts give you credit for.
reflectionPrompt: When you look back on past hardships, how did navigating them expand your capacity for strength?
